newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria deal with oil firms long way off - Shell.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria deal with oil firms long way off - Shell.

text.p: Negotiations between Nigeria and its joint venture partners on a new Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) remains far from being concluded, the outgoing chief executive of Shell Nigeria said on Monday.
"We are still talking with the government on the MOU and we still have a long way to go," Brian Anderson told a news briefing in Lagos.
"It is very important to the upstream oil business that a properly constituted and attractive MOU is negotiated and implemented for everybody," Anderson said.
The existing MOU came into being in 1991 and lapsed in 1996. It guaranteed a profit margin of $2.50 per barrel of crude to the oil producing companies.
The oil firms have asked the government to raise the margin to $5 a barrel to take account of inflation and numerous taxes and levies they have to pay in Nigeria.
"We need all the incentives to prosecute the programmes on the ground," Anderson said.
He said for Shell, the programmes included ending gas flaring from its oil fields.
"By (the year) 2008 our target is to go down to near zero level of gas flaring. Already we went down by 40 percent last year," he said.
But this would depend on an appropriate investment climate in the country, Anderson said.
